content.overview: Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India. The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States (Article 89) and acts as President or discharges the functions of the President in the contingencies provided in Articles 65 and related provisions.
content.glance: There shall be a Vice-President of India — ex officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha; acts as President when required.
content.study:
Article 63 is the constitutive provision for the office of Vice-President. Linked provisions: election (Art 66), term (Art 67), qualifications (Art 66), oath (Art 69), and discharge of Presidential functions (Art 65). As Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Art 89), the Vice-President is a key parliamentary officer.

Examination: constitutive provision; link to Art 89 (Chairman) and Art 65 (acting President).

sections.heading: Key point
sections.body: There shall be a Vice-President of India. Ex officio Chairman of the Council of States; acts as / discharges functions of President under Art 65.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 63 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India. The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States and acts as President or discharges the functions of the President in the situations provided in the Constitution.

examTips: VP office created; ex officio RS Chairman.

keyTakeaways: Art 63: there shall be a Vice-President of India.
